title: Prop: no fill since 2026-08-30, and the status ask fires on the wrong trigger
note: OPERATOR-RAISED 2026-09-21, unprompted, in their own words: 'I haven't gotten any trade notifications there in a suspiciously long time, and I keep getting the prop status request notifications even though we said we don't need that anymore -- I give the snapshot when a trade closes and the account doesn't need to be tracked actively when there's no activity.' [!] MEASURED off the live host the same hour (direct over ict-bot.duckdns.org, not from a doc): newest account_status is id 19 at 2026-08-30T19:33:29Z -- status_age_hours 528.4 against a 24h threshold, freshness `stale`. distance_to_dd_floor_usd reads $87.34 against the $4,700 static floor, computed off that 22-day-old snapshot; distance_to_daily_loss_usd is null (day_pnl_state `realized_unreported`), so the daily-loss half of the account-killer guard is NOT COMPUTED AT ALL. Newest ticket 2026-09-13 `expired`; everything back to 2026-08-30 `suppressed`/`skipped`. reconcile: 92 tickets, 43 fills, 0 unacted. [!] SO THE STRATEGY SIDE IS ALIVE AND NOTHING REACHES A FILL -- that is the shape of the question, and the lane's first job is to say WHICH of four candidates is true with a stated population, not to adopt the tidy one. The manager's leading hypothesis (sizing refusing on the stale balance) is EXPLICITLY CHALLENGED on the row: a ticket was emitted 2026-09-13, fourteen days past the snapshot, so sizing did not refuse on that tick. [!] OPERATOR DECISION 2026-09-21 (popup, direct): the status ask fires ONLY ON NEW EXPOSURE -- at the moment a real, non-suppressed ticket is about to take exposure. The flat-book cadence goes. They were shown the $87.34-on-a-22-day-old-number cushion and the cost of going quiet while flat, and chose this. prop_status_request.py's docstring argues WELL against it (the static-DD floor binds while flat); that argument is to be KEPT and the decision recorded beside it, dated and attributed -- not deleted. [!] OPERATOR CONFIRMED, asked directly: breakout_1 is funded, live, and SHOULD be trading. So the silence is a defect, not the expected state. [!] THE PIPELINE PREDICTED THIS EXACT DAY. BL-20260909-PROP-SIZING-REFUSAL-ON-A-STALE-BALANCE-IS-JOURNALED-BUT-NEVER-PINGED has been open since 2026-09-09 and its clears_when says in terms: 'breakout_1 can stop trading indefinitely with the only evidence being a journalctl line.' The operator found it from the outside, by noticing an absence of notifications -- the worst available discovery method, and the second time today that the operator's own eyes beat a sweep. [!] SO SILENCING THE ASK DOES NOT SHIP ALONE: the periodic ask was the only thing that happened to be noisy in the stalled state, so removing it makes the silent stall strictly worse. The refusal path gets an operator-facing signal in the same landing. [!] LANE FENCED OUT of changing sizing logic, breakout_executor's suppression rule, and anything on the order path -- a diagnosis pointing there comes BACK as a proposal. PROP IS REAL MONEY: routed to opus for that reason, against the model table's order-path line. [!] MERGED 2026-09-21 as 635600c, Tier-2, OPERATOR APPROVED after being shown what it does. [!] THE ROOT CAUSE IS FOUND AND IS NOT WHAT ANYONE GUESSED -- and the manager's leading hypothesis (sizing refusing on the stale balance) was REFUTED twice, independently. TWO INDIVIDUALLY-CORRECT TIER-3 CHANGES COMPOSED INTO A SILENT OUTAGE: 2026-08-23 removed the base twins from breakout_1's roster (approved de-dup), and 2026-08-31 rewrote _election_sort_key so the base twin now wins a tie against its _prop sibling. The twins carry IDENTICAL entry parameters, so both fire on every breakout bar, one global winner is elected per symbol, and since 2026-08-31 the winner is always the base twin -- which is not on breakout_1. MEASURED 21 of 21 contested packages to the base twin; breakout_1 received none. No ticket, no suppressed row, no rejection, no log line naming the account. [!] THE ASK WAS A LATCH, established before anything was changed: a 2026-09-13 ticket with a 1h TTL expired unanswered, `expired` was not in NON_EXPOSING_TICKET_STATUSES, and the arm compared against a snapshot only an OPERATOR REPORT can move -- so it asked every 12h forever for the report it was asking for. Fixed as a class (`ticket_can_take_exposure`), not as an instance. [!] landed_unproven, NOT done: BL-20260909 is MOVED not closed (its clears_when needs the refusal observed reaching a channel on the live host after deploy), and the OUTAGE ITSELF IS UNFIXED -- that is E17. [!] CLOSING THIS ROW MEANS TWO OBSERVATIONS, AND THEY ARE SEPARATE. (a) The status ask: a 12-hourly prop status-request ping does NOT arrive while the book is flat and no ticket can take exposure -- the operator noticing its ABSENCE over a few days, since the fix is the removal of a signal and there is nothing positive to see. (b) The sizing-refusal page: a `prop_sizing_refusal` observed reaching an operator-facing channel on the live host after deploy, which is BL-20260909's own clears_when and currently unmakeable while the diag relay is down (E19). ⚠️ NEITHER closes the OUTAGE -- breakout_1 receiving a ticket again is E17. [2026-09-25 sweep] (a) Live state (diag log_file prop_status_request) shows the last ask fired on last_verdict=position_open, matching the new trigger, not cadence -- but breakout_1 hasn't been flat long enough since the fix to observe an absence; recheck once it goes flat for >=48h. (b) operator_alerts.jsonl (2026-09-18 to 09-25, direct diag read, 301 entries) has zero prop_sizing_refusal or any prop-kind entries -- no refusal event has occurred to test the channel. Note: E19 is actually done and the diag relay is directly reachable (verified this session) -- (b)'s blocker is that the triggering event hasn't happened, not the relay.
